reason: Missed calls on a job do cost me work, and I'm glad I keep my number. But my appointments already live in my scheduling/CRM tool, and this only texts me or books into Google Calendar, so I'd end up retyping every lead on Sunday night. That's a second system, and I'd be paying $2,000 up front just to get it.
objection: It doesn't plug into the software I already run my jobs in, and $1,999.99 before I've seen a single lead is a lot for a one-person shop when there's no live transfer on urgent calls.
would_change_my_mind: If it pushed the caller's details and bookings straight into my existing scheduling/CRM tool, with the setup fee cut or credited back after a trial month where I see it catch real jobs.
